_comment: Drafted replies keyed by tweet id. Edit freely; the review page reads these as starting text and sends whatever is in the box.

replies.2092427029727916415: The 30 nanometre figure is the real headline, not the 95 percent. Worth pressing on "no new waste stream" though: adsorption concentrates PFAS rather than destroying it, so regenerating the powder should leave a concentrated eluate that still has to go somewhere.
replies.2092413047948386313: It is certified to NSF 42, 53 and 401, which genuinely beats most pitchers: 53 covers lead and PFAS, 401 covers microplastics. What it is not is 58, the reverse osmosis standard. Keeping the minerals is the same property that leaves fluoride and nitrate in.
replies.2092556408747425822: There is a specific reason to expect that association even at zero causal effect. Tumour vasculature is leaky and disorganised, so circulating particles accumulate there preferentially. Higher levels in cancerous tissue can be downstream of the tumour, not upstream.
replies.2092643242126852216: The trap is what people buy next. Ceramic nonstick is a sol gel coating that wears faster than PTFE, so it gets replaced more often, and PFAS free on the box refers only to the coating. Bare stainless or cast iron is the version with nothing to wear off.
replies.2092616379299951101: The direction of the effect is what makes this hard to summarise. Depending on ageing and surface chemistry, plastics can either shuttle cadmium toward roots or sequester it away from them. Does the review land on which dominates under field conditions?
replies.2092450662227591602: The polymer backbone is the easy part. What decides whether this is edible is the additives: plasticisers, antimony catalyst residue from PET, flame retardants. Those do not necessarily break down in the same step, and they are what would need clearing.
replies.2092875350984241294: The mechanism is the interesting part. PLA softens at a far lower temperature than PE, so a hot drink sits above its glass transition point and the lining degrades while you drink it. Compostable describes the end of life, not what happens at 80 degrees.
replies.2092992982865596491: That is the rare thing in this field: a dated baseline. Museum series let you date when contamination started rather than only measuring the present, which is the control almost every microplastic study is missing.
replies.2092981126176379066: RO does remove them from the source water. The catch is what happens next: PET sheds into its own contents, and warehouse and truck heat speeds that up. You are buying clean water and then storing it in the contamination source.
replies.2092742418948829201: For what it is worth, swallowed flakes are the least bad version of this. PTFE is inert enough that it mostly passes straight through. The actual hazard is heating an empty pan past about 260C, which is when the coating starts breaking down into fumes.
replies.2092880041143320841: The intervention half is where these reviews usually thin out. Most proposed strategies target the microbiome rather than the particles, which means measuring a downstream marker and calling it mitigation. Does this one commit to an endpoint?
replies.2092994279547245045: The detail that catches people out is superwash wool. It is finished with a polymer resin to stop it felting, so machine washable merino sheds like a synthetic while being sold as the natural option.
replies.2095477938560827887: The specific problem is duration. Those liners are nylon or PET held near 95C for six to ten hours, in fat and acid. Migration testing is mostly built around minutes of heating, so the everyday slow cooker case is the one least studied.
replies.2095425984736497982: It is certified to NSF 42, 53 and 401, which genuinely beats most pitchers. What it is not is 58, the reverse osmosis standard, so fluoride, nitrate and arsenic stay in. Solves most issues would be fair. All of them is doing a lot of work.
replies.2095504225430057225: Worth keeping two findings apart here. The 2025 testing that found lead in about 90 percent of 51 toothpastes was measuring contamination carried in by mined mineral abrasives, not fluoride. Different cause, different fix, and conflating them muddies both.
